x: Technological unemployment from automation and AI mainly hits low-skilled, routine jobs.

s: Where is technological unemployment mainly found?
x: Technological unemployment, a subtype of structural, is predominant in manufacturing and routine services.

s: Which of the following may still exist at full employment?
o: Involuntary unemployment of those willing at the prevailing wage
x: Full employment means everyone willing at the prevailing wage finds work, but frictional and structural unemployment may persist.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Educated unemployment is mainly rural.
2. Seasonal and disguised unemployment are mainly rural.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Seasonal and disguised unemployment are major rural forms, while educated unemployment is predominantly urban.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India – mainly structural and disguised unemployment
Developed countries – mainly structural and disguised unemployment
x: India's unemployment is mainly structural and disguised, while developed countries mainly face cyclical, demand-deficient unemployment.

s: A fall in the measured unemployment rate may not show real job creation when it results from which of the following?
o: A rise in potential GDP caused by technology
A permanent reduction in the labour force due to higher wages
x: A falling unemployment rate may reflect people entering low-productivity work under distress rather than the creation of good or adequate jobs.

s: Which type of unemployment is India's basic unemployment problem?
x: India's problem is structural, with seasonal, disguised and underemployment, unlike the demand-deficient unemployment Keynes stressed for developed economies.

s: Which of the following explains the structural nature of unemployment in India?
o: Only seasonal rainfall variations and tourism cycles
High labour mobility, labour-intensive production and low population growth
Rapid population growth, labour immobility and a shift towards capital-intensive production
Short job-search periods and temporary workplace transfers
x: Rapid population growth, labour immobility and the shift towards capital-intensive production contribute to a long-run shortfall of labour demand relative to supply.

s: Which of the following is a structural cause of unemployment in India's secondary sector?
o: Abundant job creation in labour-intensive industries
Slow infrastructure and delays in official paperwork
x: Slow infrastructure and paperwork delays are identified structural impediments; expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing would reduce unemployment, and MSMEs have been neglected.

s: Jobless growth is more likely when economic growth is driven mainly by which of the following?
o: Labour-intensive manufacturing rather than capital-intensive activities
Capital-intensive sectors such as information technology and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing
x: Growth led by capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance, instead of labour-intensive manufacturing, can produce jobless growth.

s: What is India's projected skilled-labour surplus by 2030?
x: India is a labour-surplus economy with a projected skilled-labour surplus of about 245.3 million by 2030.

s: About what share of India's workforce is informal?
x: About 90% of India's workforce is informal, one of the causes behind its unemployment problem.

s: According to the monthly PLFS (CWS), what was India's unemployment rate in May 2026?
x: The monthly CWS rate rose to 5.5% in May 2026 from 5.2% in April.

s: About how many seasonal labourers migrate in India every year?
x: About 30-35 million seasonal labourers migrate every year (September 2026), a sign of seasonal unemployment in rural areas.

s: According to Keynes, what is the main cause of unemployment in developed economies?
o: A mismatch caused only by technological change
x: Keynes explained unemployment in developed economies mainly through deficiency in effective demand, which is associated with demand-deficient or cyclical unemployment.

s: Which types of unemployment make up the natural rate of unemployment?
x: The natural rate is the combination of frictional and structural unemployment existing at full employment.

s: According to Okun's law, what is a one percentage point rise in unemployment above the natural rate associated with?
o: A 2% rise in output above potential GDP
A 1% rise in output above potential GDP
A 2% fall in output below potential GDP
A 5% fall in output below potential GDP
x: Okun's law states that a one percentage point increase in unemployment above the natural rate is associated with roughly a 2% reduction in output below potential GDP.

s: Who among the following is associated with the concept of the natural rate of unemployment?
x: The concept of the natural rate of unemployment is associated with Milton Friedman.

s: In which situation does the traditional trade-off between inflation and unemployment break down?
o: Stable prices with potential output growth
Stagflation, characterised by high inflation and high unemployment
x: Stagflation combines high inflation with high unemployment and therefore breaks down the traditional Phillips-curve trade-off.

s: According to Friedman and Phelps, what is the shape of the long-run Phillips curve?
o: vertical at the natural rate of unemployment
x: The short-run curve shows an inverse unemployment-inflation link, but in the long run it is vertical at the natural rate.

s: In which year did A.W. Phillips show the inverse relation between unemployment and inflation?
x: A.W. Phillips presented the inverse unemployment-inflation relation in 1958.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Milton Friedman – natural rate of unemployment
x: Friedman is linked with the natural rate; Okun links unemployment with output, Phillips with inflation, and the vertical long-run curve is Friedman-Phelps.

s: According to PLFS 2025, the unemployment rate among youth aged 18-29 was about 14.8%. What was it for tertiary-educated youth in that age group?
x: Tertiary-educated youth recorded an unemployment rate of 29.4%, about double the overall youth rate of 14.8%. 6.5% is the rate for persons with secondary schooling and above, 11.9% is the Gen Z (15-26) rate, and 40.1% is the share of tertiary-educated youth who are NEET.

s: As per PLFS 2025, what was the unemployment rate for Gen Z (15-26)?
x: Gen Z (15-26) unemployment was 11.9%; 14.8% was for youth aged 18-29.

s: What share of India's tertiary-educated youth are NEET (not in employment, education or training)?
x: About 40.1% of tertiary-educated youth are NEET; 29.4% is their unemployment rate.

s: What is the main cause of educated unemployment in India?
x: Educated unemployment is an urban phenomenon caused by a mismatch between curriculum and industry needs.

s: According to K.P. Kannan, in which State is educated unemployment the highest?
x: K.P. Kannan found the maximum percentage of educated unemployed in Kerala.

s:
Assertion (A): Educated unemployment can rise even during a period of high economic growth.
Reason (R): Professional and job-oriented education is lacking.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Without professional education, graduates do not match the jobs that growth creates, so educated unemployment rises.

s: As per PLFS 2024-25, what was the youth (15-29) unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Youth (15-29) unemployment in Andhra Pradesh was 17.5%; urban female youth was 29.1%.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Frictional unemployment is associated with transition between jobs.
Structural unemployment involves a mismatch of skills or geography.
Institutional unemployment can arise from regulatory and policy barriers.
Underemployment refers to surplus labour with zero marginal output.
x: Surplus labour adding nothing to output is disguised unemployment; underemployment means workers not using their full skills or hours.

s: An MBA graduate working full-time as a driver at a very low income is an example of which of the following?
x: Invisible underemployment exists when a person works full-time but earns very little or works below their ability, as in the example of an MBA working as a driver.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about voluntary and involuntary unemployment?
o: Voluntary unemployment means unwillingness to work at the prevailing wage.
Involuntary unemployment means being willing to work at the prevailing wage but finding no job.
The labour force counts only voluntary unemployment.
The labour force counts only involuntary unemployment.
x: The labour force counts only involuntary, not voluntary, unemployment.

s: Persons able and willing to work but having no job at all are in which type of unemployment?
x: Open unemployment means being able and willing to work with no job at all.

s: What is working fewer than the normal hours known as?
x: Visible underemployment means fewer than normal hours; invisible underemployment is full-time work at very low income.

s: The labour force counts only which kind of unemployment?
x: Only involuntary unemployment (willing at the going wage but no job) is counted in the labour force.

s: A person unemployed for more than how many months is said to be in long-term unemployment?
x: Long-term unemployment means being unemployed for over 12 months.

s: What is the situation in which unemployment benefits discourage people from taking up work called?
x: An unemployment trap arises when benefits make work less attractive, so people stay unemployed.

s: The unemployment rates under UPS, CWS and CDS in the NSS 68th Round for 2011–12 were respectively:
x: For 2011–12, the NSS 68th Round reported unemployment rates of 2.7% under UPS, 3.7% under CWS and 5.6% under CDS.

s: What was graduate unemployment as per PLFS 2022-23?
x: PLFS 2022-23 gave 3.2% overall unemployment and 13% for graduates.

s: CWS unemployment rates exceed UPSS rates mainly because the 7-day reference period captures which type of unemployment?
x: The short 7-day CWS reference period picks up seasonal unemployment, so CWS rates are higher than UPSS rates.

s: What was the unemployment rate (UPSS) as per PLFS 2019-20?
x: PLFS 2019-20 put UR at 4.8% (APPSC 2022); 6.1% was for 2017-18.

s: What was the PLFS 2025 (calendar year) unemployment rate?
x: PLFS 2025 gave a UR of 3.1%, down from 3.6% in 2022.

s: As per PLFS 2023-24 (UPSS), what were India's rural and urban unemployment rates respectively?
x: PLFS 2023-24 put the all-India rate at 3.2%, with rural 2.5% and urban 5.1%.

s: As per the quarterly PLFS for January-March 2026, what was the urban unemployment rate?
x: The January-March 2026 quarterly PLFS gave an overall rate of 5.0%, with urban 6.6% and rural 4.3%.

s: According to the NSS 61st round (2004-05), what was India's unemployment rate on usual status basis?
x: The NSS 61st round (2004-05) put the usual status unemployment rate at 2.3%, a marginal rise from 2.2% in 1999-2000.

s:
Consider the following statements about unemployment on usual status basis:
1. It rose marginally from 2.2% in 1999-2000 to 2.3% in 2004-05.
2. The 2004-05 figure came from the NSS 68th round.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The usual status rate rose from 2.2% (1999-2000) to 2.3% (2004-05); the 2004-05 data came from the 61st round, while the 68th round was for 2011-12.

s: As reported by CMIE, approximately how many persons were unemployed in India in December 2021?
x: CMIE reported approximately 53 million unemployed persons as of December 2021.

s: Which organisation conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments?
o: Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
Directorate General of Employment and Training alone
x: The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment conducts the Employment–Unemployment Survey and the Quarterly Employment Survey of establishments.

s: In 2019, the CSO and NSSO were merged to form which body?
o: Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics
x: In 2019 the CSO and NSSO merged into the National Statistical Office (NSO).

s: Before NITI Aayog was set up, from which source were unemployment data mainly obtained?
x: Before NITI Aayog, unemployment data were primarily obtained from the NSSO. Official unemployment information was also associated with the CSO and NSSO statistical system.

s: In which year was the Labour Bureau, which conducts the EUS and QES, set up?
x: The Labour Bureau (1920) under the Ministry of Labour and Employment conducts the EUS and QES.

s: From which survey do CMIE's monthly unemployment data come?
x: CMIE is a private body that runs the monthly CPHS with a larger sample and different method.

s: From which NSS round did the quinquennial Employment-Unemployment surveys of the NSSO begin?
x: The NSSO's quinquennial Employment-Unemployment rounds ran from the 27th to the 68th round (2011-12), after which PLFS took over in 2017.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: UPS – employed if worked 90 days or more in 365 days
UPS – employed if worked 183 days or more in 365 days
UPS – employed if worked 273 days or more in 365 days
x: UPS uses a 365-day reference period and counts a person employed for the major part of it, generally 183 days or more; CWS uses a 7-day period.

s: Under the UPSS approach, a person is also counted as employed if he or she did subsidiary work for at least how many days in the 365-day reference period?
x: UPSS includes principal-status workers and those who did subsidiary work for at least 30 days during the year.

s: In the Current Daily Status approach, what is the basic time unit used for recording employment?
x: CDS uses a half-day as the unit of measurement. Four or more hours of work are treated as employment for that day.

s: Why does the Current Daily Status approach generally produce the highest unemployment rate?
o: It counts days of unemployment even for persons treated as employed under CWS.
It uses a reference period of 365 days.
It includes only persons who are not seeking work.
It excludes all seasonal workers from employment.
x: CDS records unemployment separately for each day and therefore captures intermittent unemployment that may not be reflected when a person is counted as employed under CWS.

s: Current Weekly Status (CWS) captures seasonal unemployment because it counts a person as employed if he or she worked for how long?
o: For at least 30 days in the preceding year
For at least one hour on any day during the preceding seven days
On every day of the preceding month
For at least 183 days in the preceding year
x: CWS covers a seven-day reference period and counts a person as employed if the person worked for at least one hour on any day during that period.

s: In Census terminology, for at least how many days in a year must a person work to be a main worker?
x: A person who worked for 183 days or more is a main worker; less than 183 days makes a marginal worker.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a method used by the NSSO for measuring unemployment in India?
x: Current Monthly Status is not one of the listed NSS status approaches. UPS, CWS and CDS are recognised approaches in this framework.

s: Under the CDS approach, for how long must a person work to be counted as employed for the day?
x: CDS uses a half-day unit; working 4 or more hours counts as employed for the day.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 183-day criterion:
1. It is the UPS 'major time' threshold.
2. It separates Census main workers from marginal workers.
3. The Census approach is one of the NSS status approaches.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 183 days marks both UPS major time and the Census main-worker line, but the Census is not an NSS approach.

s: Which approach of the NSSO captures both chronic and seasonal unemployment?
x: With a 7-day reference period, Current Weekly Status captures chronic as well as seasonal unemployment.

s: Which status approach gives the highest unemployment rate?
x: CDS counts days of unemployment even of persons employed under CWS, so it gives the highest rate.

s: The Unemployment Rate (UR) is unemployed persons as a percentage of which of the following?
x: UR uses the labour force as base; the proportion unemployed (PU) uses the population.

s: Which identity links the three labour indicators?
x: The worker population ratio equals LFPR multiplied by (1 − UR).

s: What are unemployed persons as a percentage of the total population called?
x: PU divides the unemployed by population, while UR divides them by the labour force.

s: What is the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)?
o: Employed persons as a share of the total population
Labour force as a share of the working-age population
Unemployed persons as a share of the labour force
Unemployed persons as a share of the total population
x: LFPR is the labour force (employed + unemployed) per 100 of the working-age population.

s: Which of the following persons are outside the labour force?
o: Persons who worked for at least one hour in the week
Students and homemakers not seeking work
x: The labour force is the employed plus those seeking or available for work; students and homemakers not seeking work are outside it.

s: On whose advice was the Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics, which designed PLFS, set up?
x: The Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics was set up on the advice of the National Statistical Commission and designed the PLFS framework.

s: When was the Periodic Labour Force Survey launched?
x: PLFS was launched in April 2017. Its first annual report, relating to 2017–18, was released in May 2019.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the PLFS revamp from January 2025?
o: Monthly all-India CWS estimates began to be produced.
Quarterly estimates were extended to rural areas.
The annual report shifted to the calendar year.
The sample was reduced to about one-half of its earlier size.
x: The sample was raised, not reduced, to about 2,72,304 households.

s: When was the first annual PLFS report, for 2017-18, released?
x: PLFS was launched in April 2017 and its first annual report (2017-18) came out in May 2019.

s: From January 2025, PLFS began releasing which estimates?
x: The 2025 revamp added monthly all-India CWS estimates and extended quarterly estimates to rural areas.

s: Before the January 2025 revamp, for which areas did PLFS give quarterly estimates?
x: PLFS quarterly estimates were for urban areas only (CWS); from January 2025 they were extended to rural areas.

s: After the January 2025 revamp of the PLFS, its sample was raised to about how many households?
x: The revamp raised the PLFS sample to about 2,72,304 households, about 2.65 times the earlier size.

s: Which was the last quinquennial NSS employment-unemployment round?
x: The 68th round (2011-12) was the last quinquennial round before PLFS.

s: How do CMIE unemployment data differ from PLFS data?
o: annual, with the same methodology as PLFS
monthly, but with a methodology identical to PLFS
based on the PLFS methodology with a smaller sample
monthly, with a larger sample and a different methodology
x: CMIE data are monthly with a larger sample and a different methodology, which makes their estimates diverge.

s: Which body conducts the Periodic Labour Force Survey?
o: The Census of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
The National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
The Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy under NITI Aayog
The Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
x: PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office, which functions under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

s: Critics argue that the CWS measure of unemployment may mask which of the following?
x: CWS is criticised for masking underemployment and missing circular migration.

s: Critics say the CWS measure misses which phenomenon?
x: CWS counts 1 hour a week as employed, masking underemployment and missing circular migration.

s: As per PLFS 2024-25, what were the rural and urban unemployment rates of Andhra Pradesh respectively?
x: In Andhra Pradesh rural unemployment was 3.4% and urban 5.9%; open unemployment is higher in urban areas.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's unemployment rate under PLFS 2023-24 (usual status)?
x: AP's rate was 4.1% against India's 3.2%; AP's rural rate (3.4%) was below its urban rate (5.9%).

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's urban unemployment rate (usual status) in PLFS?
x: AP's urban rate was 5.9% against a rural rate of 3.4% and an overall 4.1%.

s: What was the unemployment rate of urban female youth in Andhra Pradesh as per PLFS?
x: Urban female youth in AP had an unemployment rate of 29.1%; 22.7% and 15.5% were urban and rural youth rates.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh in PLFS 2023-24?
o: AP's unemployment rate was above the national rate
Urban youth unemployment exceeded rural youth unemployment
x: AP's male rate was 4.3% and female 3.7%, so female unemployment did not exceed male.

s: What was the principal recommendation of the Dantwala Committee regarding unemployment estimation?
o: To replace NSS surveys with CMIE surveys
To provide separate estimates by status and by category
To use one single national number for all forms of unemployment
x: The Dantwala Committee rejected a single-number estimate and recommended separate estimates by usual, weekly and daily status, as well as by category.

s: Which committee reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies in 1973?
o: Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics
x: The Bhagwati Committee, constituted in 1973, reviewed unemployment estimates and employment-oriented policies.

s: In which year was the Dantwala Committee on unemployment estimates set up?
x: The Dantwala Committee was set up in 1970; the Bhagwati Committee followed in 1973.
